title: Request classification and deferred execution protocol
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary ------- This decision record defines a standardized Request Classification and Deferred Execution Protocol (RCDEP) for Redwood Inference. The goal is to provide a concise, operationally-safe contract for: - Classifying incoming inference requests into deterministic handling classes. - Allowing best-effort deferred execution for low-priority work while preserving higher-tier SLOs. - Providing clear fallback semantics and audit trail for deferred or dropped requests. Scope ----- Applies to all external-facing request ingress paths and edge proxies that hand off to the serving runtime (hosted API, Dedicated ingress, and Private runtime sidecars). Does NOT change model output semantics; it only affects scheduling, admission, and fallback behavior. Motivation ---------- Redwood serves mixed workloads with widely varying latency and cost requirements. Without a consistent classification and deferred execution contract, teams implement ad-hoc timeouts and retries causing SLO violations, duplicate work, and billing surprise. RCDEP centralizes the policy so runtime, edge, and SDKs behave consistently. Design principles ----------------- - Predictability: high-tier requests must observe bounded tail latency (P99) targets. - Observability: every decision (defer, accept, reject, drop) is recorded with reason codes. - Minimal semantic change: application-visible outputs remain unchanged except when a request is intentionally degraded (see Failure modes). - Pluggable policy: teams may adopt preset policies (strict, balanced, opportunistic) per tenant. Request classification taxonomy ------------------------------- All incoming requests MUST include a Classification header (x-rw-class) set by client SDKs or edge proxies. Allowed values: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, BATCH, BACKGROUND. If missing, default to MEDIUM. Table: handling profile per class | Class | SLO priority | Accept window | Defer allowed | Typical use cases | |---|---:|---:|:---:|---| | HIGH | critical | 0–200 ms | no | interactive chat, synchronous user actions | | MEDIUM | standard | 0–800 ms | conditional | API endpoints with relaxed P99 | | LOW | best-effort | 0–2000 ms | yes | analytics, optional enrichments | | BATCH | throughput | asynchronous | yes | large embedding batches, offline re-runs | | BACKGROUND | non-urgent | hours | yes | periodic maintenance tasks | Admission and deferred execution protocol (RCDEP v1) --------------------------------------------------- 1. Ingress validation: proxy authenticates and canonicalizes request, extracts x-rw-class and x-rw-deadline-ms (client-specified deadline in ms). 2. Admission decision: the ingress consults local capacity and policy. Possible decisions: ACCEPT_IMMEDIATE, DEFER_WITH_HANDLE, REJECT (hard), QUEUE (bounded), or ACCEPT_DEGRADED (fallback model). 3. If DEFER_WITH_HANDLE: ingress returns 202 Accepted with Location header /deferred/{id} and an estimated start ETA. The request is persisted to the tenant-scoped deferred queue with metadata and reason code. 4. Deferred worker picks up requests from the deferred queue respecting tenant fairness, quotas and per-class throughput caps. Workers must read x-rw-mutability (see below) before execution. 5. On execution, service posts an event to the Audit bus and notifies the client via webhook or poll endpoint. 2xx responses include metadata: execution_time_ms, reason_code, and used_model_variant. Mutability and side-effect signals --------------------------------- - Requests with side effects (billing operations, transactional writes) MUST set x-rw-mutability: "immutable" or "idempotent". - Deferred execution is only allowed for requests marked idempotent or immutable="false" with explicit client consent. The serving runtime will reject deferral for requests marked "has-side-effects" unless configured as "allow-deferred-writes" at tenant-level. Failure modes and fallbacks --------------------------- - If deferred queue growth > 2x normal, RCDEP transitions LOW/BATCH/BACKGROUND classes to REJECT with reason_code=queue_overrun. - If worker capacity is exhausted, MEDIUM requests MAY be downgraded to ACCEPT_DEGRADED using a smaller model variant (model-quantized or fast fallback) following model-variant-compatibility matrix. - HIGH requests must never be downgraded or deferred except under explicit emergency override by SRE. Emergency actions are written to the incident log. Telemetry and observability -------------------------- Mandatory telemetry emitted for every request: - rw.request.class (string) - rw.admission.decision (ACCEPT_IMMEDIATE | DEFER_WITH_HANDLE | REJECT | ACCEPT_DEGRADED | QUEUE) - rw.reason_code (string) - rw.defer.handle_id (present for deferred requests) - rw.enqueue_latency_ms, rw.start_latency_ms, rw.exec_duration_ms - rw.model.variant (string) SLO impact and metrics guidance ------------------------------- - HIGH: P99 latency <= 200 ms, error budget 0.1%/month. - MEDIUM: P99 <= 800 ms, error budget 1%/month. - LOW/BATCH: throughput budgeted, tail latency not guaranteed. Operational runbook (high level) ------------------------------- 1. Detect: Alert on rw.defer.queue_size > threshold (tenant-scoped) or sustained growth for 10m. 2. Triage: Check reason codes (queue_overrun, capacity_surge). 3. Mitigate: Apply temporary tenant throttles, enable temporary burst capacity, or enforce automatic rejection for LOW classes. 4. Restore: Increase worker pool, rebalance deferred shards, and run backfill jobs for lost deferred items. Rollout plan ------------ - Phase 0 (canary): Implement on a single non-critical region with MEDIUM default and defer disabled. 2 weeks. - Phase 1: Enable DEFER_WITH_HANDLE for LOW/BATCH on a small set of tenants; observe telemetry for 4 weeks. - Phase 2: Gradual rollout to all regions; default policies: balanced. - Phase 3: SDK updates to attach x-rw-class and x-rw-deadline-ms by default. Example policy config (tenant YAML) | key | type | description | default | |---|---|---|---| | default_class | string | fallback class for untagged requests | MEDIUM | | allow_deferred_writes | bool | permit deferral of write-like requests | false | | deferred_queue_max_size | int | per-tenant limit for deferred queue | 10000 | Example request/response (edge)
Request headers: ``` POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1 Host: api.redwood.ai Authorization: Bearer x-rw-class: LOW x-rw-deadline-ms: 120000 Content-Type: application/json ``` Ingress response when deferred: ``` HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted Location: /deferred/ef97a2b4 Content-Type: application/json { "handle_id": "ef97a2b4", "eta_seconds": 38, "reason_code": "capacity_surge_low_class" } ``` Deferred execution event (audit bus payload): ``` { "handle_id": "ef97a2b4", "tenant": "acme-corp", "class": "LOW", "used_model": "rw-llm-7b-quant-v2", "start_ts": "2026-03-10T12:03:45Z", "duration_ms": 412 } ``` Security and compliance notes ----------------------------- - Tenant-level deferred queues must be encrypted at rest using customer or platform-managed KMS keys. - Requests containing PHI/PII MUST be tagged with x-rw-sensitive=true and are ineligible for deferred execution unless tenant policy explicitly allows. Ownership and contacts ---------------------- - Product owner: Asha Patel - Primary SRE contact: Ethan Liu - Runtime owner: María Gómez Open questions and future work ----------------------------- - Should the ingress return estimated cost delta when returning ACCEPT_DEGRADED? (action: Product) - Reconciliation guarantees for deferred durable queues: at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics (action: eng-serving-runtime). Appendix: short checklist for implementers ----------------------------------------- - [ ] Ingress sets and validates x-rw-class and x-rw-deadline-ms. - [ ] Admission emits rw.admission.decision and rw.reason_code. - [ ] Deferred queue items include idempotency token and mutability flag. - [ ] Audit bus records execution events for every deferred job. - [ ] SDKs upgraded to set default classification by Q3 2026.
